Inoculation Theory in Synthetic Media Environments
J. Smith — fabricated source document for the SlopChecker test corpus.

Abstract. Inoculation against synthetic persuasion behaves like its
attitudinal ancestor: pre-exposure to weakened arguments confers
resistance. Our central finding is that durable attitude change
requires repeated exposure across multiple framings, and that a single
framing — however strong — decays toward baseline within days.

We further show that inoculation transfers only weakly across topics,
and that booster exposures restore most of the lost resistance.
